This is HMMT problem: known answer 24.

Let me verify. Let α=√3+√2, β=√3−√2. P(α)=P(β). The minimal polynomial of α is x⁴−10x²+1, and its conjugates are ±√3±√2, with β one of them. P(α)=P(β) means P(x)−P(β)... Either degree 1 impossible (α≠β). Degree 2: Q(x)=x²+ax+b, with α+β=2√3 ≠ −a, so impossible. Degree 3: the condition is that Q(α)−Q(β) = 0 where α−β=2√2; (α−β) divides, giving (α²+αβ+β²)+a(α+β)+c(cubic: x³+ax²+bx+c) → α²+αβ+β² + a(α+β) + b = 0. Compute α²=5+2√6, β²=5−2√6, αβ=1. Sum: 11. Then a·2√3 + b + 11 = 0 gives a=0, b=−11. So Q = x³−11x + c (the a here is the x² coefficient). Degree 3 works.

Q(10)−Q(0) = 1000 − 110 = 890.

Check the cubic case of Q(x)=x³+ax²+bx+c: Q(α)−Q(β)=(α−β)(α²+αβ+β²) + a(α²−β²) + b(α−β) = 0. Dividing by α−β: 11 + a(α+β) + b = 0, with α+β=2√3, so a=0, b=−11. Correct.

So Q(10)−Q(0) = 1000 − 110 = 890.

(My initial recollection of 24 was wrong; the derivation gives 890.)

ANSWER: 890
